messages:
oncall-bot: Pager: HIGH - TLS handshake failures on inference-hostpool-3 in us-west-2. 95% of TLS connections failing (SYN succeeded, handshake timeouts). Paging routing: @sre-rotation oncall.
oncall-bot: Severity: P2. Affected customers: several small PLG apps, API error 523 from edge proxy. Runbook: /runbooks/tls-handshake-failures.
sre-rotation: Picking up. I’m in transit, give me a minute to pull logs. @alex.k can you confirm whether this is limited to us-west-2?
alex.k: I’m seeing alerts from both us-west-2 and us-east-1 but much higher in us-west-2. CPU/gpu nodes healthy. LB metrics show lots of SSL handshake errors on the NLBs fronting runtime.
samira: Reproduced locally with `openssl s_client -connect runtime-us-west2.redwood.ai:443` — hangs at "SSL_connect:errno=0" then times out after ~12s. us-east returns fine.
anya: I’m checking cert rotation timeline — we rotated leaf certs for runtime onus-west-2 ~03:10 UTC via cert-rotator service. Rotation completed without errors per logs.
maria: Customer reports: error 523 and latency spikes. Adding ticket IDs: #SUP-4432, #SUP-4433.
ops-lead: Quick mitigation: do we have fallback routing to another region or older cert pinned? Consider routing traffic to us-east.
alex.k: We can shift low-priority traffic to us-east via routing policy, but dedicated customers pinned to us-west will still fail. Propose canary switch of hostpool to previous cert in staging? Need coordination with cert-rotator.
sre-rotation: Timeline capture — posting raw events from the NLB/ELB logs and cert-rotator here.
sre-rotation: ```
# ELB logs (partial)
2026-03-15T03:09:58Z elb1 ... TLS-ALERT  140:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert unknown ca
2026-03-15T03:10:04Z elb1 ... Failed handshake  count=78 target=runtime-1
2026-03-15T03:12:02Z elb1 ... TLS-ALERT  110:SSL routines:tls_construct_server_hello
```
anya: Cert-rotator log snippet: ```
2026-03-15T03:09:50Z cert-rotator job=leaf-rotate region=us-west-2 status=initiated
2026-03-15T03:10:12Z cert-rotator job=leaf-rotate region=us-west-2 status=success cert_id=crt-9a7f
2026-03-15T03:10:13Z cert-rotator job=leaf-rotate region=us-west-2 deployed_nodes=48
```
alex.k: Hmm cert-rotator claims success immediately before the ELB TLS errors spike. Hypothesis A: new cert somehow incompatible with NLB/ALB TLS policies (cipher/chain), Hypothesis B: certs deployed to app hosts but LB still sees old chain issues (chain order/bundle wrong), Hypothesis C: MTU or VPC peering change causing TLS handshake fragmentation leading to failures.
samira: I ran `openssl s_client -connect` with `-msg` and saw handshake stuck during CertificateVerify on some nodes; on others the chain returns `unable to get local issuer certificate`.
devops-bot: Automated check: verifying certificate chain for crt-9a7f across nodes -> 52/60 OK, 8/60 failing chain order. Failing nodes: runtime-3a, runtime-3b, runtime-3f.
maria: Those failing nodes correspond to the busiest hostpool shards serving dedicated customers. That explains why dedicated tenants see more failures.
anya: Can someone paste the exact cert bundle that cert-rotator uploaded? I want to check issuer ordering.
sre-rotation: Pasting cert bundle hash: sha256:ab12... and first 512 chars of PEM...
sre-rotation: ```
-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
MIIF... (snip)
-----END CERTIFICATE-----
-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
MIIE... (intermediate)
-----END CERTIFICATE-----
```
alex.k: Chain ordering looks reversed on the failing nodes (leaf then root then intermediate). Nginx/OpenSSL expects leaf->intermediate->root or leaf->intermediate usually; some LBs have strict expectations.
ops-lead: If chain ordering is wrong, can we hotfix by re-ordering bundle on the 8 failing nodes? How fast to patch?
sre-rotation: ETA ~12m to push corrected bundle and reload runtime process. We should drain each host before reload.
anya: Also verify MTU logs — I saw an unrelated recent change where infra team toggled jumbo frames on a subnet in us-west-2 at 02:58 UTC. Could cause fragmentation during handshake. Checking VPC flow logs now.
samira: Confirmed: tcpdump on runtime-3f shows TLS handshake packets fragmented (large ClientHello with SNI + ALPN causing >1500) and subsequent retransmits. MTU on interface is 9000 but path MTU to LB is 1500; PMTU blackhole suspected.
ops-lead: Ok parallel hypotheses: cert chain ordering AND MTU fragmentation. Priority: fix cert bundle ordering (low blast radius) and then mitigate MTU.
devops-bot: Mitigation actions queued:
- Action A: reorder cert bundles on failing nodes (owner: alex.k)
- Action B: temporarily change LB to accept broken chains / lower TLS strictness (owner: ops-lead)
- Action C: revert jumbo frames on affected subnet (owner: infrastructure)
- Action D: reroute dedicated traffic to us-east for impacted customers (owner: maria)

alex.k: Starting Action A now. Will patch runtime-3a, 3b, 3f first. Draining and reload commands:```bash
kubectl cordon runtime-3a
kubectl drain runtime-3a --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
kubectl exec -n infra cert-reloader -- ./apply-bundle --node runtime-3a --bundle /tmp/cert-bundle.pem
kubectl uncordon runtime-3a
```
alex.k: Patch applied to runtime-3a and 3b, reload success, SSL handshake errors dropped ~65% on those shards. Continuing with 3f.
samira: After 3b patch, `openssl s_client` shows full chain, no more "unable to get local issuer certificate".
ops-lead: Maria, start contacting the two highest impacted enterprise customers with a status update and ETA for full mitigation.
maria: On it. Messaging drafted and sent.
anya: Infrastructure team confirms they will revert jumbo frame toggle in 8m. That should remove the fragmentation piece.
sre-rotation: After runtime-3f patched and jumbo frames reverted, error rates fell to baseline. Confirming final verification: health checks green, TLS handshake success rates back to normal.
devops-bot: Post-mitigation checks: TLS success rate 99.9% in us-west-2; no regressions in us-east-1.
ops-lead: Great. Now capture RCA notes in-thread: Root cause: Cert-rotator deployed cert bundles with incorrect chain ordering to a subset of nodes (8/60) coincident with a recent infra change toggling jumbo frames on an us-west-2 subnet. The combination caused handshake failures to spike. If cert chain had been correct, MTU fragmentation might still have caused some retries but not the widespread failures observed.
anya: Contributing factors: 1) cert-rotator didn't validate chain ordering across all nodes, 2) infra change to jumbo frames without end-to-end PMTU verification, 3) lack of Canary cross-check for cert deployment with LB-specific expectations.
alex.k: Immediate actions (postmortem tasks):
- Fix cert-rotator: add chain-order validation and deploy tests against LB parsing (owner: anya).
- Add PMTU verification step to infra 
```
